declared_debt.reason: the eligibility mask requires at least K fills in BOTH halves, so the three early per-wallet arrays it subsets are restricted to wallets that traded again after the flag would have fired. The file's own header says the late half is the prediction target only; the mask contradicts it. Left standing rather than repaired in place because the repair moves the eligible count and every figure downstream of it, which is a recompute and a re-reading of the register, not an edit

the cutoff is the argmax of true-positive minus false-positive rate over sixty candidates, scored against the late-window cost decile, and the flagged fraction reported beside it is measured at that same cutoff on that same half. The number is a fitted value, not an out-of-sample one, whatever it is called

the wallets the headline figure draws are those clearing the fill floor in BOTH halves, and the top-decile cut is taken over that survivor set. Same defect as the classifier's eligibility mask, on the figure the report leads with

the unit list keeps a wallet only when it clears the floor in both halves, which is unavoidable for a persistence correlation -- the quantity being measured is defined on pairs -- but it makes the population a survivor set all the same, and the artifact does not say so. Declared so that the limitation is written down rather than assumed harmless

the out-of-sample leg flags on the early top decile and measures late realized profit, but the wallets it ranks are those with K fills in both halves, so the flag is taken over a set the flagging moment cannot know

a counterparty with no late-half fills gets no row at all, so the feature frame this file writes is a table of wallets that came back. The frame's own leakage note covers label leakage and says nothing about this

the control reads the published delta, which mm_bakeoff.py measures on days 9 to 13, and books its own offset on those same days. What it does with the loaded value is choose which of two constructions of the early premium the published number stands on, and refuse to print a residual unless one of them reproduces it. That choice is made with a quantity from the window the file reports over, and it is the point of the file rather than a defect in it: a control that has not reproduced the published number has no baseline. Declared so that the dependence is written down instead of assumed harmless

the census prices the two-sided admission rule by reading what the producers that carry it published, so their late-half quantities are its SUBJECT and not an input to a decision it takes. Same ground as its RULE 1 entry below, and the file says so to its own artifact under deliberate_lookahead

this producer draws the appendix figure of the raw material and takes no decision at all, so RULE 4's premise -- that an arm is priced off a quantity fitted on the days it quotes over -- has no arm to attach to here. The days do meet: i3_book_comparator.py measures on days 9 to 13 and this module binds the same late half. What it binds it FOR is the right-hand panel, which draws the boundary between the two halves and prints each half's median quoted spread, so the reader can see that the split this study rests on does not sit on a regime break. That is a description of the window, not a booking across it, and RULE 4 cannot tell the two apart because both bind the same name. What makes this checkable rather than asserted is where the loaded values go: book_feats_{COIN}.npz is opened at exactly two sites and NEITHER of them reaches the picture. check_against_book_feats() recomputes the four depth columns from the raw levels and requires them to equal the committed artifact row by row, which can only stop the run and can never move a number; its result is recorded under against_a_committed_artifact and is not plotted. degeneracy_of_two_rungs() counts how often the two rungs of that file are equal, which is the measurement behind spending two and a half minutes on the raw snapshots instead, and it decides a parsing route rather than a counterparty, a cutoff or a price. Every series on both panels is re-parsed from the raw snapshots by this file. So no value fitted on the late half reaches any published quantity, and a reader can confirm it by opening the artifact and finding those two records and no third. The entry is keyed to this ONE input on purpose: a second fitted input read by the same file is a new finding and this line will not excuse it

this producer carries the admission rule as the OBJECT of a measurement rather than as the ground of a decision. Its as_committed arm rebuilds the two-sided mask on purpose, so that the price of the rule can be printed beside the two arms that relax it, and the file declares this to its own artifact under the key deliberate_lookahead. Removing the pattern would hide the very expression being priced, which is why the entry stands here instead
